title: fix(ui): restore editor type checks for native bridges and QA fixtures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ten editor typecheck errors when the UI graph includes native Mermaid tests and plain-Node QA fixtures.

## User Impact

UI editor typechecks pass. No runtime, API, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Match the existing test graphs' JavaScript inference policy, and keep the standalone Mermaid document's bridge type local to its implementation and browser test. This removes the accidental global `Window.webkit` collision without weakening the desktop gateway tests.

## Evidence

- [Baseline and repaired editor graph](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40488942486): ten errors before, zero after. The graph adds only `quota-reset-diagnostics.mjs` and `worker-heap-flag.mjs` (23,659 → 23,661 files).
- [Focused sibling and runtime proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40489452412): production and UI E2E typechecks pass; 9 diagnostics tests and 7 native browser tests pass; formatting passes. Before/after native renderer builds produce byte-identical `native.js`.
- Independent source review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final commit has the same tree as the reviewed candidate after restoring the workflow.
- Three files, +15/-9 lines: production net +1 (local bridge type), tests +3, config +2. The temporary proof workflow is restored exactly; final source files match those exercised above.

<details>
<summary>Dependency contracts checked</summary>

[TypeScript's allowJs contract](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs.html) supports inference for imported JavaScript. The unchanged fixture's [Codex token-refresh contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/account.rs#L241) was inspected directly; this patch changes no protocol behavior.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Broad CI attribution before landing</summary>

[CI run 40489965868](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40489965868) passes production/test typechecks, lint, security, and the other selected jobs. Two runtime UI jobs remain red:

- [Chat controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40489965868/job/122141836659): two cases fail the shared controls-fixture assertion. The first case and assertion also fail in [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40475262163/job/122092192541).
- [Avatar dialog](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40489965868/job/122141836945): switching avatar tabs changes measured height by 108px. Its cause remains unresolved; same-failure reproduction on baseline is not claimed.

Attribution uses the actual tested merge 58cc7cda85996941ed8f0b826c9b1d18fbfeafd5 and its first parent 22c29786817f5e94ea913a3d35568dc86d493267. Test, component, style, harness, build, and dependency inputs for these failures are byte-identical. The entire introduced delta is this three-file patch. The native declarations erase and the changed browser test does not enter either failed runtime graph.

The pinned [Rolldown 1.2.14 transform](https://github.com/rolldown/rolldown/blob/v1.2.14/crates/rolldown_plugin_vite_transform/src/utils.rs#L120) and [compiler-option merge](https://github.com/rolldown/rolldown/blob/v1.2.14/crates/rolldown_common/src/inner_bundler_options/types/tsconfig_merge.rs#L12) do not use `allowJs` for emitted code. [Resolver ownership](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc-resolver/blob/v11.24.3/src/tsconfig.rs#L638) also stays unchanged because the editor graph retains explicit TypeScript-only include patterns. These contracts exclude a runtime regression introduced by this diff.

The native unrelated-CI exception retains the failed result and exact-head evidence. These fixture/layout failures remain separate follow-ups.

</details>
